remotion.title: LeClap vs Remotion
remotion.tagline: Two ways to turn code into video, deterministically. Remotion composes with React components and renders in Node or in the browser. LeClap composes from a JSON template and links FFmpeg into the app itself, so the same template also renders natively on a phone. Here is where each one wins — including where Remotion does.

native.label: Renders in a native app, no browser engine
native.leclap: React Native, with FFmpeg linked into the app

deterministic.label: Same input, same output
deterministic.leclap: Per platform — the encoder differs, see the caveats
deterministic.remotion: By design, if the composition avoids randomness

agent.label: Authored by an AI agent
agent.leclap: MCP tools, with no LLM in the output path
agent.remotion: A system prompt teaches an LLM to write React

caveats.title: The honest caveats
caveats.leclap: LeClap's determinism holds per platform, not across platforms. Node and the browser take the libx264-style software path; the on-device build is LGPL, so Android encodes with libopenh264 and iOS with Apple's h264_videotoolbox, both driven by a bitrate target instead. The on-device filter set is narrower too: boxblur is dropped and eq is rewritten to lutyuv. Same template, same cuts, same timings — different pixels on each target.
caveats.remotion: Remotion's browser renderer carries the mirror-image caveat: it emulates layout onto a canvas rather than screenshotting a page, so it does not match its own server-side output pixel for pixel.

chooseRemotion.title: Choose Remotion when…
chooseRemotion.lead: It is the better tool more often than a comparison page usually admits.

composition.title: Your composition is really a component tree
composition.body: Hooks, spring(), interpolation, component reuse, a live in-page preview — expressive things a JSON descriptor is deliberately too narrow to say. If you are already thinking in React, Remotion lets you keep thinking in React.

scale.title: You render on servers, at scale
scale.body: Remotion has a documented, mature path for distributed and serverless rendering — a render farm you can point at a queue. LeClap has no equivalent and is not trying to build one.

ecosystem.title: You want a mature ecosystem
ecosystem.body: Years of releases, a large community, templates, an embeddable player, editor packages, and answers to questions nobody has thought to ask of LeClap yet.

web.title: Your audience is on the web
web.body: If your users are on a WebCodecs-capable browser, Remotion's client-side renderer already gives you a serverless render. The native-app gap below simply does not apply to you.

chooseLeClap.title: Choose LeClap when…
chooseLeClap.lead: The corner where the browser engine is the problem, not the platform.

native.title: The video is composed inside a native app
native.body: Capture from the camera, apply effects, mix music, add transitions, render — the whole loop runs in your iOS or Android app, with FFmpeg linked in and no browser engine anywhere in the path.

privacy.title: The media must never leave the device
privacy.body: There is no upload step to disable, because there is no upload step. Your footage never leaves the device — the render happens where the camera is.

agent.title: An agent authors the video
agent.body: The MCP server exposes schema, validate and compose as tools, so a model writes a JSON template and the engine renders it. No LLM sits in the output path: the result is rendered, not sampled.

data.title: The composition is generated by a program
data.body: A validated JSON descriptor is far easier to emit, diff, store and review than a React component you first have to compile.

sources.title: Sources
sources.lead: Every claim about Remotion above was checked against Remotion's own documentation on 14 August 2026. Something out of date or unfair? Open an issue and we will fix the table.
